transcript: 00:00:05 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give a quick status then run through the tabletop rollback scenario. Nora, Carlos, Priya — thanks for making time.

00:00:23 Nora Li: Yeah thanks Maya. we got a bunch of internal stakeholders watching this week so trying to make the rollback bit as concrete as possible, like who flips what and how long it takes to failback.

00:00:38 Jonah Ruiz: Cool. quick recap — since last week we ran the shadow routing for the latency-optimized model, saw ~18% cost savings with a 40ms median tail increase, KV cache hit-rate about 23% for prefix matches.
00:00:55 Carlos Mendes: Wait 40ms tail — that's a bit higher than we expected. is that p95 or p99? our SLA calls for p95 under 300ms.

00:01:10 Jonah Ruiz: sorry, yeah p99 tail shift. p95 stayed within 270ms for most requests. some longer conversations with >1k tokens spiked. the cost savings were driven by quantization and reduced flops on the deduped path.

00:01:30 Priya Shah: Quick security Q — when you say quantization, are there any model artifacts that leave our VPC? like, where do keys live? we need KMS integration and audit trails for any swapped artifacts.

00:01:45 Maya Patel: Good call. for the POC we're using Redwood Dedicated in a private VPC peering setup; keys are customer-managed KMS and we log all model pulls in the audit feed. we'll share the audit schema after the call.
00:02:02 Ethan Brooks (Product): also on rollback: if we do an emergency swap to the legacy endpoint, how do we avoid tokenization drift? i.e., responses shouldn't change form factor mid-session.

00:02:18 Jonah Ruiz: We recommend session fencing and soft fallbacks — the runtime can route by session ID and keep KV cache compatibility by serving a compatibility variant that maintains tokenization. there's a small quality delta but preserves format.
00:02:40 Speaker 6: (inaudible) ...i think we saw some weird spacing on the client after fallback last week — maybe token boundaries changed.

00:03:02 Maya Patel: noted, we'll add a tokenization-check step into the rollback playbook. ok, tabletop time — scenario: pilot traffic hits a regression in hallucinations detected by BrightPath eval suite at 14:22. Carlos, walk us through the infra signal you'd surface.

00:03:22 Carlos Mendes: first signal is error rate bumped and our safety-eval webhook flagged 12% of responses for a red tag. at that point we'd like to initiate an automatic canary kill and switch to the fallback. question: who has permission to flip the switch?
00:03:45 Priya Shah: from security stance we prefer a two-person approval for a full model swap — one infra owner and one product or compliance sign-off. can Redwood support RBAC for that?

00:03:59 Jonah Ruiz: yep, RBAC is supported in the console — you can require multi-approvals for rollout actions. we can also wire up an API that accepts a signed approval token to prevent accidental flips.
00:04:20 Nora Li: timeline is critical — how long to cut traffic to fallback and what happens to in-flight sessions?

00:04:34 Jonah Ruiz: typical canary kill + redirect to fallback (soft routing) is sub-2m for new sessions. in-flight sessions get a TTL-based drain — you can choose immediate cut or let them finish within a per-session grace window. in practice, we saw 90% session preservation with a 30s drain.

00:04:58 Maya Patel: important trade here — immediate cut reduces exposure faster but increases UX friction. BrightPath, which is more important for you in this pilot: lowest risk or lowest user disruption?
00:05:12 Nora Li: safety first for sure. users are clinicians, so hallucinations are our top concern even if a small number of sessions drop.
00:05:28 Maya Patel: okay safety-first default, we'll set the abort policy to immediate-by-default with a 60s grace that you can override. action item to capture that in the runbook.
00:05:43 Ethan Brooks: also want to understand rollback verification — after swapping, how do we confirm the fallback reduced the error rate without reintroducing other regressions?

00:05:58 Jonah Ruiz: We'll run a targeted eval subset against the fallback within the canary window and surface a pass/fail metric. plus the console will show token-level diffs and quality flags so you can sanity check before clearing the incident.

00:06:15 Priya Shah: on the audit side, we need the full timeline of who executed the swap, the model versions involved, and the pre/post eval artifacts. can you include an exportable incident packet?
00:06:31 Maya Patel: yes, the incident packet includes model version IDs, rollout policy, traces and the safety evals we ran. i'll attach a sample packet to the follow-up email.
00:06:47 Nora Li: switching gears — model selection. Jonah, can you summarize your recommendation between the two pinned sets we discussed?

00:06:58 Jonah Ruiz: Sure. Option A is latency-optimized: 8-bit quantized variant, slight p99 tail uplift but 25–30% cost saving. Option B is quality-optimized: FP16-ish variant with more conservative quantization, better QA pass rates but cost ~18% higher.
00:07:18 Nora Li: we ran a specialty safety eval and quality-optimized passed 93% while latency-optimized hit 86% on the clinical prompts set. that gap matters to us.

00:07:32 Maya Patel: recommendation: pin quality-optimized for the initial pilot stable path, keep latency-optimized in a shadow route for 2 weeks if you want to test economics. we can use soft fallback rules to go to quality immediately on any safety flag.
00:07:50 Carlos Mendes: from infra side, if we keep the latency variant shadowed, what's the extra egress or cost overhead? we care about peak GPU utilization and burst caps.

00:08:05 Jonah Ruiz: shadowing is read-only — you pay for inference for the shadowed tokens but it's cheaper than full traffic. estimate for your 10k tpm pilot: shadow adds ~12% to GPU cycles on peak; we'll give a detailed cost split in the spreadsheet.
00:08:25 Priya Shah: one more question on private deployment: if we ever need to do an on-prem emergency swap, is the model artifact the same or do we need to pull a different binary?

00:08:40 Jonah Ruiz: We provide compatible artifacts for private deployments. there are two bins: a quantized runtime and a default runtime. both are pinned with a version hash so swap is just a config change if artifacts already cached. otherwise, model pull could add time — which is why we recommend caching the fallback images during readiness checks.

00:08:59 Maya Patel: real-world drill: we will simulate a failure at 14:22, infra kills canary at 14:24, fallback in by 14:26, verification by 14:30. that's a 8-minute window. BrightPath wants to run this next Friday — Carlos, are we good to include on-call infra?
00:09:19 Carlos Mendes: yes, we'll have infra on-call and will run the peering tests before the drill. I'll also confirm egress rule exceptions for the pull so we don't block the swap.
00:09:33 Nora Li: for acceptance criteria for the pilot: reduce hallucination red tags below 2% in production or we won't move to Dedicated. can Redwood provide a contractural metric for that?
00:09:47 Maya Patel: we can include a pilot success metric in the SOW addendum — let's capture the exact wording and threshold in the next steps. action: Maya will propose language.
00:10:02 Ethan Brooks: small note — client libraries saw a minor header mismatch when we tested cross-origin routing. not sure if that's Redwood or our gateway. We'll attach the client logs.
00:10:13 Jonah Ruiz: send them over, we saw a similar header normalization edge case last quarter — likely the gateway stripping a custom accept-type. we can add an adapter in the runtime if needed.
00:10:28 Priya Shah: last item: compliance packet. can we get SOC2 evidence and the last three months of pen-test summary?
00:10:41 Maya Patel: yes we'll share SOC2 report excerpt and the pen-test summary redacted — posting to the secure SSO link. action item for me in the follow-up.
00:10:55 Nora Li: perfect. anything else from Redwood?
00:11:01 Jonah Ruiz: one thing — we'll attach two JSON examples for canary policies: immediate-cut and staged-cut. BrightPath can pick one as the default for the pilot.

00:11:12 Maya Patel: recap of next steps: maya send pinned model config + SOW language, jonah export traces and push canary policy samples, priyasha confirm SOC2 window; carlos run peering tests and schedule the tabletop for 2026-11-12. does that match?
00:11:32 Nora Li: yes that matches. thanks everyone — we'll review the artifacts and confirm the drill time via calendar invite.
00:11:44 Maya Patel: great — thanks all. we'll follow up with the packet and the spreadsheet. meeting over.
00:11:50 (call ended)
